messages.text:
We propose the following terms for the pilot.

- **Color calibration.** For the first batch, we request written approval for one external color specialist to view selected full-resolution master images. Seeing the whole sheet helps the specialist judge color variation across the paper. We’ll identify the specialist before access, bind them to the studio’s confidentiality and deletion terms, and provide a view-only account with downloads disabled. Access will expire when calibration is complete or five calendar days after access begins, whichever comes first. If full sheets are too sensitive, we can use full-resolution crops of archive-approved areas of blank paper and include the color target from the same scan.
- **Corrections and deletion.** Only the assigned studio operators and quality reviewer will have access to working files, apart from the specialist’s limited access above. We propose ten calendar days after delivery of each batch for the archive to report defects. For any defect reported in that window, we’ll retain only the affected files for up to ten further calendar days from the report to correct and redeliver the scans. We’ll delete working copies when each applicable window closes, or sooner if the archive accepts the batch in writing. Encrypted backups will be restricted to recovery administrators and will expire through rotation within 45 calendar days after working-copy deletion. If a backup is restored in that interval, we’ll reapply the deletion. We’ll confirm the working-copy deletion date and the final backup expiry date in writing.
- **Publicity.** We’d like to publish one anonymized photograph of the scanning process on the studio website. We propose framing the equipment and color target so no handwriting, donor identifiers, or collection labels are visible, and stripping identifying metadata. We’ll submit the exact image and caption for separate written approval before publication. If the archive declines, we’ll delete the proposed publicity image with the batch working files.

Would the archive approve the limited full-sheet review, or should we plan around crops? We’d also like to confirm whether ten days from batch delivery gives the archive enough time to flag defects.

Ten calendar days from delivery of each batch gives the archive enough time to report defects. For calibration, please plan around an archive-supplied calibration sheet. We propose the following terms for the signed schedule.

- **Access and calibration.** The archive will flag two restricted collections before transfer. Only the assigned studio operators and quality reviewer may view their handwriting or identifying content. Exclude both collections from specialist review. If the calibration sheet proves insufficient, tell us what the specialist still needs to assess. For other collections, the archive may approve full-resolution crops of blank paper with the color target from the same scan. Supply only flattened, masked images with identifying metadata removed. The archive must approve the named specialist and exact images in writing before access. We accept the proposed confidentiality terms, view-only access, disabled downloads and five-day maximum, with access ending sooner when calibration finishes. Full-sheet donor masters are outside this approval.
- **Corrections and deletion.** Delete working copies ten calendar days after batch delivery, or sooner on written acceptance. For a defect reported within that window, retain only the affected files for correction and delete them on acceptance of the correction or ten calendar days after the report, whichever comes first. Please cap encrypted backup retention at **30 calendar days after working-copy deletion**. Limit backup access to recovery administrators and reapply deletions before restored files return to use. For each batch, provide dated written confirmation when working copies have been deleted and again when the last backup containing them has expired.
- **Incident contact.** Enter a monitored incident email and an urgent phone number for each party in the schedule before signing. The studio should notify the archive contact within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, then follow up with the affected batch, known scope and containment steps.
- **Publicity.** The archive may approve one equipment-only photograph for the studio website. Stage it with the materials and color target removed and screens blank. Strip identifying metadata and submit the exact image and caption for separate written approval before publication. Delete any unapproved photograph with the batch working files.

Please confirm the 30-day backup cap or identify the shortest rotation you can support. Any longer period would need an express exception in the signed schedule.

The shortest backup rotation we can support is **45 calendar days after working-copy deletion**. We request this express exception in the signed schedule:

> For each pilot file, the studio will ensure that the last encrypted backup containing that file expires within 45 calendar days after deletion of its working copy. Only recovery administrators may access backups, solely for recovery. The studio will reapply deletions before restored files return to use. For each batch, the studio will provide dated written confirmation when all working copies have been deleted and a second dated confirmation when the last backup containing batch files has expired.

We accept the ten-day review and correction windows and earlier deletion on written acceptance as proposed. We also accept the incident contact and 24-hour notification terms, and the equipment-only photograph conditions, including separate written approval of the exact image and caption before publication.

We’ll use the archive-supplied calibration sheet first. If it proves insufficient, we’ll identify what the specialist still needs to assess. Any donor-derived images proposed for specialist review will be limited to the specified crops from unrestricted collections, subject to all proposed masking, approval and access controls.

Can the archive approve the 45-day exception on that basis?

The archive approves the **45-calendar-day backup exception** as drafted. Please include the quoted clause in the signed schedule. The deadline runs separately for each file from deletion of its working copy. The two dated confirmations are due per batch, one after all working copies are deleted and one after the last backup has expired.

Please include the agreed calibration, access, correction, incident notification and publicity terms. Recovery access must preserve the viewing restriction on the two flagged collections. No other exception is outstanding. The remaining item before signature is for each party to supply its monitored incident email and urgent phone number.

We’ll include the approved backup clause verbatim in the schedule, together with the agreed calibration, access, correction, incident notification and publicity terms. During recovery, administrators may restore encrypted files. Only the assigned studio operators and quality reviewer may view handwriting or identifying content from either flagged collection, including during a restore.

Please supply the archive’s monitored incident email and urgent phone number for the signature copy. We’ll provide the studio’s verified contacts and sign once both parties’ details are entered.

Please leave the archive’s monitored incident email and urgent phone number blank in the signature copy pending verification. The archive will supply both before signing. All substantive terms are agreed. Only the parties’ verified contact details remain outstanding.
